## Detailed Findings

#### 1. Kilocode #13896: session list crash fix when no project context — guard for non-project invocations (SMALL priority, verify Alexi)

- **What**: Kilocode CLI's `kilo sessions list` crashed when invoked outside a project directory (no git root, no `.kilo/` or `.kilocode/` config) because the session manager tried to resolve a project-relative path without a fallback for the no-project case. Fix (PR #13896 by esc) changes the list operation to enumerate sessions across ALL projects in the sessions directory (~/.kilo/sessions/ or equivalent) instead of crashing, so `kilo sessions list` becomes a global inventory command rather than project-scoped.
- **Why**: Users who run `kilo sessions list` from their home directory or a non-code directory (e.g. to see all active sessions before deciding which project to cd into) hit an unhandled exception. The session storage is user-global (one sessions dir per user, not per project), so listing should work from anywhere.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13896 (fix(cli): list sessions across all projects instead of crashing)
- **Category**: command (session management)
- **Size**: SMALL priority, ~1h. Alexi's `ax sessions list` command (src/cli/commands/sessions.ts) uses `SessionManager.list()` (src/core/sessionManager.ts). Verify that `SessionManager.list()` handles the no-project case (e.g. when called with no workdir, no git root, or outside a repo). If it throws or filters incorrectly, apply Kilocode's fix pattern: when no project context is available, list ALL sessions from the base sessions directory (~/.alexi/sessions/) instead of filtering by project. Test by running `ax sessions list` from /tmp or ~/ (outside any repo).

#### 2. Kilocode #13818: TUI toast wrapping fix — prevent multi-line toasts from clipping after the first line (SMALL priority, defer/context only)

- **What**: Kilocode TUI's toast notification component was clipping messages longer than ~44 columns to the first line instead of wrapping, because the Box only set `maxWidth` (a Yoga flex constraint) but not `width` (the actual width Ink's Text uses to determine line breaks). Multi-line messages like 'The running Cline Hub stays on the cline hub upgrade' rendered as 'The running Cline Hub stays on the' and never showed the critical instruction. Fix sets explicit `width={Math.min(message.length + border + padding, maxWidth)}` so the Text component knows where to wrap.
- **Why**: Toasts are ephemeral notifications that must deliver their full message in the short time they are visible. Clipping after the first line makes them useless for multi-sentence instructions (Hub upgrade reminders, error recovery steps, keyboard shortcut hints).
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13818 (fix(cli): make TUI toasts wrap instead of clipping after the first line)
- **Category**: command (TUI rendering)
- **Size**: SMALL priority, DEFER. Alexi does not currently render toasts in the TUI (no Toast.tsx or notification component in src/cli/tui/components/). If future work adds a toast/notification surface, follow Kilocode's pattern: set explicit `width={Math.min(messageLength + paddingAndBorder, maxWidth)}` on the Box wrapping the Text. NOT immediately actionable.

#### 13. Kilocode #13734: host-bridge auth token — secure local bridge calls with spawn token (LOW priority, Cline/host-specific)

- **What**: Cline (Kilocode's internal name before rebranding) Host Bridge (localhost gRPC bridge between the core and the IDE host) now requires an authentication token (`CLINE_CORE_CONNECTION_TOKEN` sent as `cline-hostbridge-token` header) on every call. Previously the bridge listened on localhost with no auth, so any local process or OS user could dial the port and drive the IDE. Fix reuses the existing spawn token (issued by the host when spawning the core) as the bridge credential, covering every path the core reaches the bridge (generated service clients, startup health check, core connection stream).
- **Why**: Unauthenticated localhost bridges are vulnerable to local privilege escalation (malicious process on the same machine can invoke IDE commands, read files, or exfiltrate secrets by calling the bridge). Token auth closes the gap.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13734 (feat(hostbridge): send the spawn token on host bridge calls)
- **Category**: config (security, host-bridge auth)
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP. Alexi has no Host Bridge, no gRPC localhost surface, no CLINE_CORE_CONNECTION_TOKEN. This is Kilocode/Cline-specific (their architecture separates the core from the IDE host via a bridge; Alexi is a single-process CLI with no bridge). Not CLI-portable.

#### 14. Kilocode #13817: run_commands background-child pipe handling — complete commands when background children hold stdio pipes (MODERATE priority, possible Alexi benefit)

- **What**: Kilocode's shell executor (run_commands tool) was hanging on commands that background a child (e.g. `cmd &`, `nohup cmd`, Git Bash on Windows equivalent) because the executor settled commands on the child process `close` event, which fires only after stdio streams drain. A backgrounded child inherits the pipe write-ends, so the shell exits but the streams stay open and `close` never arrives — the command hung until the timeout killed the whole tree. Fix: when the process has exited and the streams stay open past a 1-second grace period, settle with the exit code and output collected so far, append a note that background processes are still running, and unref the stream handles so the host process is not kept alive.
- **Why**: Backgrounding a long-running process (e.g. `npm run dev &`) is a common agent workflow. Without the fix, the agent waits for the timeout (often 2+ minutes) even though the shell returned immediately. The 1-second grace period is long enough to capture normal commands (close follows exit within milliseconds) but short enough to unblock backgrounded commands fast.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13817 (fix(core): complete run_commands when background children hold the stdio pipes)
- **Category**: tool (bash/shell executor)
- **Size**: MODERATE priority, DEFER. Alexi's bash tool (src/tool/tools/bash.ts) and shell executor may have the same issue (hanging on backgrounded children until timeout). Verify whether Alexi's shell executor waits on `close` or on `exit` + stream-drain. If it waits on `close`, apply Kilocode's fix pattern (settle on exit + 1s grace, append background-job note, unref streams). Test by running `ax chat` with a backgrounded command (e.g. `sleep 60 &`) and confirming the tool returns immediately rather than hanging for 60s or timing out. Defer to dedicated investigation (MODERATE size, ~3-4h to verify + patch + test).

#### 15. Kilocode #13827: Windows session import path resolution — fix session import paths on Windows (LOW priority, Windows-specific)

- **What**: Kilocode's session import logic (loading sessions from disk) was breaking on Windows due to path resolution bugs (likely backslash vs forward-slash, drive-letter handling, or HOMEDRIVE/HOMEPATH fallback). Fix canonicalizes paths (collapses `.`, `..`, empty segments) and preserves the Windows drive-root and runtime-home fallback paths.
- **Why**: Session import is a startup operation; if it fails, the agent cannot load history and acts as if all sessions are new. Windows users were stuck in a first-run loop every launch.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13827 (fix(core): resolve session import paths correctly on Windows)
- **Category**: config (session management, path handling)
- **Size**: LOW priority, DEFER. Alexi's session import (src/core/sessionManager.ts) uses Node's `path.join` and `path.resolve`, which should be cross-platform. If Alexi users on Windows report session-load failures, investigate path canonicalization (ensure backslashes and drive letters are handled correctly). Not immediately actionable (no Windows bug reports yet).

#### 16. Kilocode #13829: desktop backend startup off UI thread — prevent desktop backend startup from blocking the UI (LOW priority, desktop-specific)

- **What**: Kilocode desktop app's backend startup (initializing the local agent server, loading plugins, connecting to the Hub) was running on the UI thread, freezing the app for 1-2 seconds on launch. Fix moves startup to a background thread and queues incoming requests until the backend is ready.

- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13829 (fix(desktop): keep desktop backend startup off the command path)
- **Category**: config (startup performance, threading)
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP. Alexi has no Electron desktop app, no UI thread. This is desktop-specific. Not CLI-portable.

#### 17. Kilocode #13816: silent shell-integration success reporting — report silent shell commands as empty output, not failure (LOW priority, VS Code-specific)

- **What**: Kilocode VS Code extension's terminal command executor (VscodeTerminalProcess) was misclassifying silent successful commands (exit 0, no output) as shell-integration failures. When a command like `git add -A` (on a clean tree) completed with exit 0 and no output, the executor treated the empty capture as a shell-integration failure, read a clipboard snapshot of the terminal, and reported the command as failed with a dirty snapshot. Fix gates the snapshot fallback on the CommandExecuted marker: if the OSC 633 marker was seen, empty output is a genuine silent success.
- **Why**: Silent success is common (git add on clean tree, $null, mkdir when dir exists). Misclassifying these as failures breaks agent workflows that depend on git/file operations.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13816 (fix(vscode): report silent shell-integration successes as empty output)
- **Category**: tool (shell executor, terminal integration)
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP. Alexi has no VS Code extension, no terminal shell-integration surface. This is VS Code-specific. Not CLI-portable.

#### 20. Kilocode #13835: apply_patch overwrite guard — refuse to Add File over existing files (SMALL priority, verify Alexi)

- **What**: Kilocode's apply_patch tool's Add File operation was silently overwriting existing files because `loadFiles` (the pre-check step) only pre-loaded UPDATE/DELETE targets, so the parser's 'File already exists' guard never saw ADD targets and `fs.writeFile` replaced files. Fix loads existing ADD targets too so the guard fires and the tool refuses to overwrite.
- **Why**: Overwriting an existing file during Add File is almost always a mistake (the patch was generated against an older tree state where the file did not exist, or the LLM hallucinated an Add when it should have been an Update). Silent overwrite destroys uncommitted work.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13835 (fix(core): make apply_patch Add File refuse to overwrite existing files)
- **Category**: tool (apply_patch safety guard)
- **Size**: SMALL priority, ~1h. Alexi's apply_patch tool (src/tool/tools/apply-patch.ts) may have the same issue. Verify that the Add File operation (when applying a unified diff with `--- /dev/null` or equivalent new-file marker) checks `fs.existsSync(targetPath)` and refuses to overwrite. If missing, add the guard before the `fs.writeFile` call. Test by generating a patch that adds an existing file and confirming the tool rejects it with a clear error.
